text: The Intoxication of the Ulstermen is an Irish literary text. Its Irish title is Mesca Ulad. It comes from the Ulster Cycle. King Conchobar mac Nessa convinced his foster sons Cúchulainn and Fintan to let him rule their lands for a year. At the end of that time he went to honor the return of the lands. He would spend the first part of the evening with Fintan in the west. He would spend the second part with Cúchulainn. By halfway through the night the warriors were too drunk to find Cúchulainn's fortress. They came instead to the fortress of their enemy Cú Roí. He tried to trap them in an iron house he set on fire. Cúchulainn found his guests missing and freed them. The Ulstermen then destroyed Cú Roí's palace. Like other drunken tales, this one takes place at Samhain, the winter feast on November 1.
objective: Document the Irish literary text Intoxication of the Ulstermen.
key_results: Record the text as part of the Ulster Cycle.
Retell the tale of Conchobar, Cúchulainn, and Cú Roí.
Note the setting at Samhain on November 1.
